thread.title: Is Facebook’s thud a bad omen for FAANG stocks?

author: Simon Maierhofer
title: Is Facebook’s thud a bad omen for FAANG stocks?
text:
Before Thursday’s brutal action for Facebook’s stock, the “FAANG-tastic” five, as I like to call them, had driven the tech-heavy Nasdaq and Nasdaq-100 to all-time highs. Even the S&P 500 Index of the largest U.S. stocks came within 1% of setting a record.
The FAANG stocks are Facebook FB, -19.33% Amazon.com AMZN, -2.45% Apple AAPL, -0.03% Netflix NFLX, +0.07% and Google holding company Alphabet GOOG, +0.15% GOOGL, +0.45%
For the most part, things have been looking good for the FAANG group, but there are some negative signs.
Mark Hulbert: Watch out for analysts’ avalanche of price-target cuts on Facebook’s stock
Not all is good under the hood The June 15, 2018, Profit Radar Report published the chart below (left portion) and said: “The Nasdaq-100 QQQ, -1.34% appears to be nearing the end of a 5-wave advance — next resistance: 181.80, which would be followed by a larger pullback (target: 164-168).”
The chart excerpt on the right includes the most recent price action. Here are the key points:
• The Invesco QQQ Trust Series I reached the upside target at 181.80 (this is a Fibonacci projection level going back to the 2002 low).
• RSI-2 (a measure of short-term relative strength) is overbought, which increases the risk of a pullback.
• RSI-35 (a measure of longer-term relative strength) failed to confirm the new high. This is considered a bearish divergence, indicative of internal weakness.
• On balance, volume also failed to confirm the new high.
Keep in mind that all this happened even before Facebook reported earnings and dropped 20% in after-hours trading Wednesday.
Caveats and conclusion Based on the above chart and indicators, risk is elevated and greater than the upside potential.
I always analyze many different indicators, and evaluate each based on their recent and historic track record. Therefore, it should be mentioned that bearish divergences, although a harbinger of bad news historically, didn’t mean much in 2017.
Only persistence above the 181.80 resistance level would postpone the red flags waived by the indicators above, and potentially open the door for a 2017-like outcome.
